questions.question_text: The vitamin essential in tissue culture medium is
questions.explanation: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) is a vital component often required in plant and animal tissue culture media for cell growth and metabolism.

questions.question_text: Ginkgo biloba is used for its
questions.explanation: Ginkgo biloba contains ginkgolides which act as potent platelet-activating factor (PAF) receptor antagonists.

questions.question_text: The amount of barbaloin present in Aloe vera is
questions.explanation: Aloe vera typically contains about 2 to 2.5% of barbaloin, a key anthraquinone glycoside.

questions.question_text: Sildenafil is used for treatment of one of the following Disorders:
questions.explanation: Sildenafil is a PDE5 inhibitor that is approved for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension.

questions.question_text: Cardiac glycosides have the following configuration in the aglycone part of the steroid nucleus
questions.explanation: Naturally occurring cardiac glycosides possess a $5\beta, 14\beta$-cis-trans-cis steroid nucleus configuration between rings A/B and C/D.

questions.question_text: Quassia wood is adulterated with
questions.explanation: Brucea antidysentrica is a common adulterant of Quassia wood due to similar bitter principles and appearance.

questions.question_text: Eugenol is present in
questions.explanation: Eugenol is the major phenolic constituent found in Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum) and clove oil.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs is prescribed for the treatment of Philadelphia chromosome positive patients with chronic myeloid leukemia?
questions.explanation: Imatinib is a targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor specifically designed to treat Philadelphia chromosome-positive CML.

questions.question_text: Which of the following monoclonal antibodies is prescribed for patients with non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma
questions.explanation: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody used widely in non-Hodgkin's lymphoma treatment.

questions.question_text: Identify the drug which is NOT used in the treatment of malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum:
questions.explanation: Primaquine is used to clear liver hypnozoites in P. vivax and P. ovale, not as a primary treatment for acute P. falciparum blood-stage malaria.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs does NOT act through G-Protein coupled receptors
questions.explanation: Insulin acts via a receptor tyrosine kinase, whereas epinephrine, dopamine, and TSH act via GPCRs.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs is most effective in preventing transmission of HIV virus from the mother to the foetus
questions.explanation: Zidovudine (AZT) was historically and remains standard in protocols for reducing mother-to-child vertical transmission of HIV.

questions.question_text: Improvement of memory in Alzheimer's disease is brought about by drugs which increase transmission in
questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is associated with a deficit in central cholinergic transmission, treated with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following non-opioid analgesic is a prodrug
questions.explanation: Nabumetone is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory prodrug that is metabolized in vivo to its active acidic form, 6-methoxy-2-naphthylacetic acid.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs is NOT a typical anti-psychotic agent
questions.explanation: Risperidone is an atypical antipsychotic (second-generation), whereas chlorpromazine, haloperidol, and flupentixol are typical (first-generation).

questions.question_text: Which one of the followings is a plasminogen activator
questions.explanation: Streptokinase acts as a thrombolytic by directly activating plasminogen into plasmin.

questions.question_text: Myasthenia gravis is diagnosed with improved neuromuscular function by using
questions.explanation: Edrophonium is a short-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used in the Tensilon test to diagnose myasthenia gravis.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs specifically inhibits calcineurin in the activated T-Lymphocytes
questions.explanation: Tacrolimus (and cyclosporine) binds to immunophilins to inhibit calcineurin, whereas sirolimus inhibits mTOR.

questions.question_text: The chemical behaviour of morphine alkaloid is
questions.explanation: Morphine is amphoteric due to the presence of a basic tertiary amino group and an acidic phenolic hydroxyl group.

questions.question_text: At physiological pH the following compound would be MOSTLY in the structure: CC(C)C1C(N2C1(S)CC2=O)C(=O)O
questions.explanation: Penicillins have a carboxylic acid group with a pKa around 2.5-3.0, meaning at physiological pH (~7.4) they exist predominantly as anions.

questions.question_text: Which one of the followings is used as a mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder and also in certain epileptic convulsions?
questions.explanation: Sodium valproate is widely used both as an anticonvulsant and as a mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: An isosteric replacement for carboxylic acid group is
questions.explanation: Tetrazole is a classic acidic bioisostere for the carboxylic acid group, sharing similar pKa and planar properties.

questions.question_text: The given antibiotic is an example of ansamycins
questions.explanation: Rifampicin belongs to the ansamycin class of antibiotics characterized by an ansa structure (an aromatic ring bridged by an aliphatic chain).

questions.question_text: For glyburide, all of the following metabolic reactions are logical EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Glyburide is mainly metabolized via aromatic oxidation of its cyclohexyl ring and O-demethylation of the methoxy group, not amide hydrolysis.

questions.question_text: The effects observed following systemic administration of levodopa in the treatment of Parkinsonism has been attributed to its catabolism to dopamine. Carbidopa, can markedly increase the proportion of levodopa that crosses the bloodbrain barrier by

options.A: Increasing penetration of levodopa through BBB by complexation with it
options.C: Decreasing metabolism of levodopa in the CNS
options.D: Decreasing clearance of levodopa from the CNS

questions.explanation: Carbidopa is a peripheral aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase inhibitor, reducing peripheral conversion of levodopa to dopamine.

questions.question_text: Ethambutol molecule has
questions.explanation: Ethambutol has two identical chiral carbons, giving rise to 3 stereoisomers (d, l, and meso forms).

questions.question_text: A compound will be sensitive towards IR radiation only when one of the following properties undergo transition on
questions.explanation: A molecular vibration is infrared active only if it causes a net change in the dipole moment of the molecule.

questions.question_text: X-ray crystallographic analysis of an optically active compound determines its
questions.explanation: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction with anomalous dispersion can determine the absolute three-dimensional configuration of chiral molecules.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is WRONG

options.A: A singlet or triplet state may result when one of the electrons from the HOMO is excited to higher energy levels
options.B: In an excited singlet state, the spin of the electron in the higher energy orbital is paired with the electron in the ground state orbital
options.C: Triplet excited state is more stable than the singlet excited state
options.D: When the electron from the singlet excited state returns to ground state, the molecule always shows fluorescence phenomenon.

questions.explanation: Deactivation of a singlet excited state can occur via non-radiative pathways (like heat dissipation or intersystem crossing) as well as fluorescence.

questions.question_text: Aminotransferases usually require the following for their activity
questions.explanation: Pyridoxal phosphate (PLP, the active form of Vitamin B6) is the essential coenzyme for all aminotransferase (transaminase) reactions.

questions.question_text: Purity of water can be assessed by determining one of its following properties instrumentally
questions.explanation: Electrical conductivity is a direct, highly sensitive instrumental measure of ionic impurities and purity in water.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is WRONG

options.A: Carbon NMR is less sensitive than proton NMR
options.C: Both 13C and 1H have same spin quantum numbers
options.D: The gyromagnetic ratio of 1H is lesser than that of 12C

questions.explanation: The gyromagnetic ratio of 1H is actually much larger than that of 13C, and 12C has zero spin.

questions.question_text: In the TCA cycle, at which of the following enzyme-catalyzed steps, incorporation of elements of water into an intermediate of the cycle takes place
questions.explanation: Aconitase catalyzes the reversible hydration-dehydration steps interconverting citrate, cis-aconitate, and isocitrate.

questions.question_text: Humectants added in cosmetic preparations generally act by
questions.explanation: Humectants (like glycerin and propylene glycol) attract and retain moisture through strong hydrogen bonding with water molecules.

questions.question_text: In the mixing of thymol and menthol the following type of incompatibility occurs
questions.explanation: Mixing thymol and menthol results in eutectic formation, leading to liquefaction (a physical incompatibility).

questions.question_text: Bloom strength is used to check the quality of
questions.explanation: Bloom strength is the standard measure of the gel strength and quality of gelatin.

questions.question_text: The characteristic of non-linear pharmacokinetics include

options.A: Area under the curve is proportional to the dose
options.C: Area under the curve is not proportional to the dose
options.D: Amount of drug excreted through remains constant

questions.explanation: Under non-linear (capacity-limited) pharmacokinetics, AUC is not directly proportional to the administered dose.

questions.question_text: In the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules, the Schedule relating to GMP is
questions.explanation: Schedule M of the Indian Drugs and Cosmetics Rules outlines Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for pharmaceutical products.

questions.question_text: Thioglycolic acid-like compounds have applications in following type of cosmetic formulations
questions.explanation: Thioglycolic acid and its salts are widely used in chemical depilatories to break disulfide bonds in hair keratin.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a flocculating agent for a negatively charged drug
questions.explanation: Multivalent cations such as aluminium chloride are used as flocculating agents to reduce the zeta potential of negatively charged suspensions.

questions.question_text: The healing agent used in hand creams is
questions.explanation: Urea is commonly incorporated into hand creams and ointments for its keratolytic and moisturizing/healing properties.

questions.question_text: Measurement of inulin renal clearance is a measure for
questions.explanation: Inulin clearance is the gold standard clinical measurement for determining the glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

questions.question_text: Highly branched three dimensional macromolecules with controlled structures with all bonds originating from a central core are known as
questions.explanation: Dendrimers are radially symmetric, highly branched, treelike nanoscale macromolecules emanating from a central core.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the commonly used bulking agent in the formulation of freeze dried low dose drug products?
questions.explanation: Mannitol is widely used as a bulking and crystalline matrix-forming agent in lyophilized (freeze-dried) parenteral products.

questions.question_text: The applicability of Noyes-Whitney equation is to describe
questions.explanation: The Noyes-Whitney equation quantitatively describes the rate of dissolution of solid particles in a liquid medium.

questions.question_text: Which filler can NOT be used for the preparation of tablets for amine containing basic drugs to avoid discoloration of the tablets?
questions.explanation: Lactose contains a reducing sugar group that undergoes Maillard browning reactions with primary and secondary amines, causing discoloration.

questions.question_text: The ability of human eye using illuminated area to detect a particle is limited to
questions.explanation: Under normal visual inspection with good illumination, the human eye can typically resolve particles down to about 40-50 microns.

questions.question_text: What quantities of $95\%\text{ v/v}$ and $45\%\text{ v/v}$ alcohols are to be mixed to make $800\text{ mL}$ of $65\%\text{ v/v}$ alcohol?

options.A: $480\text{ mL}$ of $95\%$ and $320\text{ mL}$ of $45\%$ alcohol
options.B: $320\text{ mL}$ of $95\%$ and $480\text{ mL}$ of $45\%$ alcohol
options.C: $440\text{ mL}$ of $95\%$ and $360\text{ mL}$ of $45\%$ alcohol
options.D: $360\text{ mL}$ of $95\%$ and $440\text{ mL}$ of $45\%$ alcohol

questions.explanation: Using alligation: parts of 95% = 65-45 = 20; parts of 45% = 95-65 = 30. Ratio is 2:3. Thus, 2/5 of 800 = 320 mL (45%) and 3/5 of 800 = 480 mL (95%).

questions.question_text: The role of borax in cold creams is

options.B: To provide fine particles to polish skin

questions.explanation: Borax reacts with free fatty acids in beeswax to form sodium soaps in-situ, acting as an emulsifying agent in cold creams.

questions.question_text: Choose the right combination

options.D: Palmitic acid, salicylic acid, fatty acids

questions.explanation: Reserpine is a classic indole alkaloid possessing antihypertensive properties.

questions.question_text: Triterpenoids are active constituents of
questions.explanation: Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri) contains active triterpenoid saponins known as bacosides.

questions.question_text: Alkaloids are NOT precipitated by
questions.explanation: Millon's reagent is a specific test for proteins and phenolic compounds (like tyrosine), not a general alkaloidal precipitating reagent.

questions.question_text: Anisocytic stomata are present in
questions.explanation: Belladonna leaves typically feature anisocytic (cruciferous) stomata surrounded by three subsidiary cells of unequal size.

questions.question_text: Bacopa monnieri plant belongs to the family
questions.explanation: Bacopa monnieri belongs to the family Scrophulariaceae (or Plantaginaceae in newer APG systems, but classically Scrophulariaceae).

questions.question_text: Tropane alkaloids are NOT present in
questions.explanation: Lobelia inflata contains piperidine alkaloids (such as lobeline), whereas Datura, Duboisia, and Erythroxylum contain tropane alkaloids.

questions.question_text: Guggul lipids are obtained from
questions.explanation: Guggul is the oleo-gum resin obtained from the plant Commiphora wightii.

questions.question_text: An example of N-glycoside is
questions.explanation: Adenosine is a nucleoside featuring a glycosidic bond between a sugar and a nitrogen atom of adenine (N-glycoside).

questions.question_text: One mg of Lycopodium spores used in quantitative microscopy contains an average of
questions.explanation: One milligram of powdered Lycopodium spores contains an average constant of approximately 90,000 spores used in quantitative microscopy.

questions.question_text: Select the correct combination of drugs for the treatment of patients suffering from Hepatitis C
questions.explanation: Combination therapy of pegylated interferon alfa and ribavirin has been a foundational treatment protocol for chronic Hepatitis C.

questions.question_text: ALISKIREN acts by

options.A: Inhibiting the conversion of Angiotensin I to II
options.C: Inhibiting the binding of Angiotensin II to the receptor

questions.explanation: Aliskiren is a direct renin inhibitor, preventing the enzymatic cleavage of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I.

questions.question_text: Digitalis toxicity is enhanced by co-administration of
questions.explanation: Quinidine displaces digitalis from tissue binding sites and reduces its renal clearance, significantly enhancing digitalis toxicity.

questions.question_text: The rate limiting step in cholesterol biosynthesis is one of the followings:
questions.explanation: The reduction of HMG-CoA to mevalonic acid by HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting step in cholesterol biosynthesis.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drugs is withdrawn from the market due to torsade de pointes
questions.explanation: Astemizole was withdrawn or severely restricted globally due to its potential to cause QT prolongation and fatal torsades de pointes.

questions.question_text: Ganciclovir is mainly used for the treatment of infection caused by
questions.explanation: Ganciclovir is an antiviral agent specifically indicated for serious cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections.

questions.question_text: Identify the one rational combination which has clinical benefit:
questions.explanation: Amoxicillin combined with clavulanic acid is a classic rational combination where clavulanate protects amoxicillin from beta-lactamase degradation.

questions.question_text: Stevens Johnson syndrome is the most common adverse effect associated with ofthe following category of drugs
questions.explanation: Sulfonamides are well known for causing severe cutaneous adverse reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

questions.question_text: Amitriptyline is synthesized from the following starting material
questions.explanation: Although multiple routes exist, phthalic anhydride derivatives or related multi-step aromatic precursors are classically taught in foundational synthesis pathways for tricyclics.

questions.question_text: The common structural feature amongst the three categories of anti-convulsant drugs Barbiturates, succinimides and hydantoins is
questions.explanation: Barbiturates, succinimides, and hydantoins all share a cyclic ureide (acylurea) core structure responsible for their anticonvulsant activity.

questions.question_text: Nicotinic action of acetylcholine is blocked by the drug
questions.explanation: d-Tubocurarine is a classic competitive neuromuscular blocker that blocks nicotinic receptors at the skeletal neuromuscular junction.

questions.question_text: Chemical nomenclature of procaine is
questions.explanation: Procaine chemically is the ester of 4-aminobenzoic acid and 2-diethylaminoethanol, named 2-diethylaminoethyl 4-aminobenzoate.
